title: 1946 London County Council election
summary: The first London County Council election after the Second World War produced a Labour landslide, mirroring the party's 1945 general election triumph. Labour won 94 of the 124 elected seats on 55.0% of the vote, with the anti-socialist Municipal Reform bloc reduced to 30. Turnout was very low at 26.4% so soon after the war.
highlights: The Municipal Reform (Conservative) bloc falls to 30 seats

council.note: 124 directly elected councillors, plus aldermen chosen by the council. The main anti-Labour party at this election was the Municipal Reform Party; the Conservatives stood under their own name from 1949. Seat shares are taken from Rallings & Thrasher's record of LCC results.

sources.label: Rallings & Thrasher, London County Council Elections 1889–1961 (Elections Centre)
